text: Crimthann was a name borne by several Irish kings. The Christian saint who later became Colum Cille, the missionary scholar, also used it. Three Crimthanns stand out above the rest. Crimthann of Tara drew a queen's eye with his charms. Crimthann Mór mac Fidaigh ruled as a king of Tara. Crimthann Nia Náir died at the battle named Intoxication of the Ulstermen.

okr.objective: Crimthann is a name shared by several Irish kings and the saint Colum Cille.
key_results: Several kings of Ireland bore the name Crimthann.
The Christian saint Colum Cille also carried the name.
The three most important figures are Crimthann of Tara, Crimthann Mór mac Fidaigh, and Crimthann Nia Náir.
Crimthann Nia Náir died in the battle of the Intoxication of the Ulstermen.
